{"findings": [{"file": "src/ev/loop.zig", "line": 385, "severity": "major", "category": "correctness", "title": "The new "no timer lock needed" claim on updateNow ignores the cross-thread setTimer", "body": "The comment added to `updateNow` states: "Owner-thread only, so no timer lock: the cross-thread `clearTimer` never reads `now`/`tick`." `clearTimer` is not the only cross-thread entry point that touches this state. `Loop.setTimer` (src/ev/loop.zig:622) calls `self.state.updateNow()` at line 636 and then `armTimer` -> `nowFor` (line 420), both under `timer_mutex`, and the repo's own test drives it from a foreign thread: "clearTimer racing a firing timer (cross-thread)" at src/ev/test/timer.zig:232 calls `loop.setTimer` on the main thread while the runner thread runs `loop.poll(.max)`, and its comment at line 241 calls `setTimer` a thread-safe API. The field doc at src/ev/loop.zig:269 also says the mutex "Protects all timer heaps and the cached `now` values", which the new comment directly contradicts.

Mechanism: `poll` now runs `updateNow` twice without the lock (line 1392, added by this change, and line 1429). `updateNow` does a non-atomic read-modify-write `self.tick +%= 1` plus plain writes to `now[0]`/`now_tick[0]`. A concurrent `setTimer` performs the same read-modify-write while holding `timer_mutex`. The mutex therefore excludes nothing, and the two increments can be lost against each other.

Consequence: a lost `tick` increment leaves `now_tick[idx] == tick` for a `boot`/`real` slot that was filled in an earlier scan, so `nowFor` returns a cached wall-clock value instead of re-reading it. A `.duration` timer armed from that value is backdated and fires early - the same defect class the poll-side refresh in this commit exists to prevent. It is also a data race by the language rules and is TSan-reportable in the existing cross-thread timer test. Either take `timer_mutex` in the two `poll` call sites, or narrow `setTimer`'s contract to owner-thread-only and fix the test and the `timer_mutex` doc to match."}, {"file": "src/ev/loop.zig", "line": 1392, "severity": "minor", "category": "tests", "title": "The new top-of-poll snapshot refresh has no regression test", "body": "This change adds `self.state.updateNow()` before `checkTimers` in `poll`, so a timer whose deadline passes during the caller's task batch is now seen by the very next `poll` instead of one iteration later. Before the change, the top-of-poll `checkTimers` scanned against the snapshot taken at the end of the previous `poll`, which is stale by the whole task batch.

No test covers the new behaviour. The one adjacent regression test, "duration timer armed after a long idle poll is not backdated" (src/ev/test/timer.zig:303), exercises the post-poll refresh at line 1429 and passes both with and without the new line, so it cannot detect a revert. The gap is observable: arm a `.duration` timer through `loop.add`, spin outside the loop past its deadline, then call `poll(.zero)` once. With the refresh the timer fires on that poll; without it `should_poll` is false, `timed_out` is false, the second `checkTimers` is skipped, and the timer only fires on the following poll. A test in that shape would pin the refresh point that this commit deliberately moved."}]}
